# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
- **IPv4:** 10.11.26.183
- **MAC:** d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b
- **Windows hostname:** DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (domain: nemotoads.health, DC NEMOTODES-DC)
- **Logged-in user:** oboomwald (confirmed via Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic to the DC at 10.11.26.3)

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** (misused legitimate remote-access tool repurposed as a trojan). **Attribution: signature-confirmed** — Suricata/ET fired `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, and `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` against the same flow. This is corroborated behaviorally: the POST bodies to the C2 use the literal NetSupport client protocol (`CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex>`), and the host separately queried the vendor's own geolocation service `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` and fetched `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp`, which is standard NetSupport client startup behavior.

## Delivery chain (behavioral, TLS-encrypted so no file hash recoverable)
1. t=32.8s: DNS lookup and TLS session to `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) — 3.5 MB exchanged.
2. t=35.7s–62s: repeated DNS lookups and TLS sessions to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139, ETPRO alert "ZPHP Domain") — the largest conversation in the capture (~11 MB), consistent with a fake cracked-software/mod-APK lure site delivering the RAT installer over HTTPS.
3. t=67s: first NetSupport RAT geolocation checkin, followed immediately by sustained C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 for the remainder of the capture (~52 min).
All three of the above sites were served exclusively over TLS; no plaintext executable was observed in the capture, so no delivered-file name or SHA256 can be grounded in the evidence.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — sustained HTTP-over-443 POST beaconing (`/fakeurl.htm`), confirmed by ETPRO NetSupport RAT CnC signatures; ~132 packets over 52+ minutes.

**Malicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` (resolves to 193.42.38.139) — ETPRO "ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup" and "ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI" alerts; largest data conversation in the capture, consistent with malware delivery.
- `classicgrand.com` (resolves to 213.246.109.5) — visited immediately prior to modandcrackedapk.com in the same infection window; part of the redirect/delivery chain.
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (resolves to 104.26.1.231, 104.26.0.231, 172.67.68.212) — NetSupport RAT's own geolocation lookup service, confirms client identity.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 checkin URI, repeated POSTs with `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` bodies.
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — NetSupport RAT geolocation request, GET.

**Files / hashes**
- None recoverable. All delivery-site traffic (classicgrand.com, modandcrackedapk.com) was TLS-encrypted; `--export-objects http` yielded only benign items (Windows connectivity test, Adobe update-check text file, OCSP response, and the small C2 `fakeurl.htm` response bodies) — no transferred executable was captured in plaintext.

## Benign context (not indicators)
Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update traffic (windowsupdate.com, smartscreen, msn.com, office.net, login.live.com, wns.windows.com), Adobe update checks (acroipm2.adobe.com, armmf.adobe.com), Google/Bing/jQuery/CDN traffic, SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR local discovery, and normal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to the domain controller 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODES-DC).

## Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as user oboomwald, was infected with NetSupport RAT after browsing to a fake cracked-software/mod-APK site (classicgrand.com → modandcrackedapk.com, 193.42.38.139) shortly after 04:49 UTC on 2024-11-26. Within seconds the malware began sustained C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 via `/fakeurl.htm`, confirmed by multiple ETPRO Suricata signatures for NetSupport RAT, and continued checking in for the remainder of the ~54-minute capture.
